Killed subpath matrices are similar to symmetric bipartite matrices, so their positive continuants decrease in survival. Reflection and a midpoint ratio exhaust every path with at most six edges. The first possible seven-edge central case reduces to a quadratic whose strict one-crossing is equivalent to b>(1+A)/(3-A); an explicit positive-rate rational example attains it. The package checker independently passed 801 exact assertions, but infinite/all-parameter coverage rests on analytic inequalities.

value.rationale: This answers the precisely motivated smallest-instance part of a published open question about finite-reset-intensity extrema in nonhomogeneous birth–death splitting. It gives the exact onset size, full necessary-and-sufficient two-parameter inequality and a closed-form optimum for every environment at the first eligible site, rather than merely a finite numerical counterexample. It connects competing short return paths to reset-control efficacy; larger path classifications remain open.
